reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that magnetron sputtering of a Ti/Ni coating on diamond particles and subsequent SPS with an HEA matrix forms a beneficial diffusion interphase that improves bonding and reduces defects. However, the evidence is for a diamond/HEA system with a Ti/Ni bilayer, not a W–Cu system with a Ni-only coating, and it does not address thermal conductivity, irradiation stability, or the specific Ni–W–Cu intermetallic formation claimed.
premises: Magnetron sputtering can deposit a thin Ni-rich coating on a particulate phase
A Ni-rich coating on a reinforcement phase can react with the matrix during SPS to form a diffusion-based interphase
Such an interphase improves interfacial bonding and reduces interfacial defects (cracks, micro-holes)
The improved interface leads to enhanced composite density and mechanical properties
